card.name: Samba
card.tagline: Brazil's iconic Afro-Brazilian dance and music.
card.profile: Samba is the iconic Afro-Brazilian music-and-dance genre. Its rural forms (notably samba de roda, Bahia) fed the urban 'samba carioca' of early-20th-century Rio de Janeiro, which became central to Carnival and a symbol of Brazilian national identity. Samba no pe is a solo footwork dance improvised to samba music; samba-enredo drives samba-school parades. Percussion includes surdo, tamborim, pandeiro, cuica and agogo (English Wikipedia).
card.insight: Folklorist Oneida Alvarenga and writer Mario de Andrade documented samba's rural roots; samba de roda was the first Brazilian musical genre IPHAN registered as national heritage (English Wikipedia).

steps.name: Basic Samba Step
steps.description: Step back on one, small step forward on two, bring feet together on three.

common_mistakes: getting confused with the coordination of the arms
safety: keep your hands to your hips to avoid confusion
lessons.teacher_style: The teacher provides clear, step-by-step instructions with a focus on weight transfer and rhythm. She maintains a friendly, encouraging tone throughout the lesson.
lessons.distinctive_method: The teacher explicitly differentiates the footwork technique for men and women, providing specific advice for each.
what_works: The teacher breaks down the movement into simple, manageable parts.
The use of slow-motion demonstrations helps the viewer understand the footwork.
what_hinders: The lack of a mirror view might make it harder for some to follow along.
